business_requirement.objective:
KMITORA 1,000-Customer Complex Address Migration DEV Test

1. Process all 1,000 customers from the connected CSV, XML and TXT customer master sources.
2. Consolidate customer master records across all source formats using customer_id as the business key.
3. Process all 2,850 customer address-history records from the connected CSV, XML and TXT sources.
4. Correlate address records to customers using customer_id.
5. Preserve every historical address record and its source lineage.
6. Never delete historical addresses.
7. Resolve operational current address as of 2026-09-19.
8. Trim leading and trailing whitespace.
9. Use uppercase normalized values for comparison.
10. Remove punctuation differences when comparing addresses for duplicates.
11. Standardize postal codes as six-digit Indian postal codes.
12. A candidate address is effective only when effective_from is less than or equal to 2026-09-19.
13. A candidate address is effective only when effective_to is blank or greater than or equal to 2026-09-19.
14. Invalid postal codes must not be promoted as the current address.
15. City and state are mandatory unless deterministic enrichment is available.
16. CURRENT address has highest operational precedence.
17. TEMPORARY address has precedence after CURRENT.
18. COMMUNICATION address has precedence after TEMPORARY.
19. PERMANENT address has precedence after COMMUNICATION.
20. WORK address has precedence after PERMANENT.
21. OTHER address has lowest precedence.
22. Prefer verified records over unverified records.
23. KYC_PORTAL has source priority 5.
24. CORE_BANK has source priority 4.
25. BRANCH_APP has source priority 3.
26. CRM_LEGACY has source priority 2.
27. KUBERA has source priority 1.
28. When conflicting candidates remain, use address-type precedence first.
29. When conflicting candidates remain, prefer verified over unverified.
30. When conflicting candidates remain, prefer the latest effective_from.
31. When conflicting candidates remain, prefer the higher source priority.
32. When conflicting candidates remain, prefer the latest source_updated_at.
33. Duplicate normalized addresses from different source systems must be consolidated logically while preserving all lineage.
34. Future-dated addresses must remain in history but must not become current before their effective date.
35. Expired temporary addresses must not be selected as current.
36. Missing effective_to means open-ended when effective_from is valid.
37. Overlapping temporary addresses must be flagged when the rules cannot deterministically resolve them.
38. An unverified newest address must not replace a valid verified address solely because it is newer.
39. Invalid postal-code records must be routed to exception handling.
40. Missing city or state must be deterministically enriched only when reliable reference data exists; otherwise route to review.
41. Temporal gaps in address history must be preserved and identified.
42. Back-dated corrections with higher version or later correction timestamp supersede earlier records for the same effective period.
43. Returning to a previously used address must be treated as a new effective-period record rather than deleting history.
44. When permanent and temporary addresses begin on the same day, temporary represents current stay while permanent remains the legal address.
45. When a customer has only a valid permanent address, permanent becomes the operational current address.
46. If no usable current address exists, mark the customer as an exception and do not invent an address.
47. Every selected current address must preserve selected_address_id.
48. Every selected current address must preserve source_system provenance.
49. Every selected current address must include the decision reason.
50. Load all valid customer identities into customer_master.
51. Load all retained historical address rows into customer_address_history.
52. Load the resolved current-address projection into customer_current_address.
53. Route invalid, ambiguous and unresolved address records to migration_exception.
54. Only validated records may be written to the DEV target.
55. Source systems must remain read-only.
56. Production writes are prohibited.
57. Production cutover is prohibited.
58. Reconcile customer identity count against the expected total of 1,000.
59. Reconcile address-history population against the expected total of 2,850 source history rows.
60. Reconcile current-address decisions against the supplied golden expected target.
61. Reconcile exception handling against the supplied expected exception file.
62. Generate evidence for source lineage, transformations, rules applied, selected address, rejected alternatives, exceptions, target load and reconciliation.
